# Challenges - Split Package - Multiple Versions

Split package happens when the same package (for example: `demo.domain`) is
found in  more than one JAR file (for example the `domain-v1.jar` and
`domain-v2.jar`). This can  happen for various reasons, the most common of which
is when different versions of the same library are found in the class path.

Another example of split package happens when JAR file *B* intentionally
contains a package with the same name as found in JAR file *A*, so that it
replaces behaviour or gains access to the default (*package-private*) classes in
JAR file *A*.

Split package are not supported by the Java Module System, and the same package
cannot be found in more than one module. This applies to all types of modules
(*unnamed*, *automatic* and *named*). Note that here we need to make a
distinction between modules and JAR files. While the relation between
*automatic* modules and *named* modules to JAR files is 1:1, there is only one
*unnamed* module, and this can **contain** more than one JAR file. All JAR files
that are found on the class path (`--class-path`) are placed in the *unnamed*
module, irrespective whether these are regular JAR files (with**out** the
`module-info.java` file) or modular JAR files (**with** the `module-info.java`
file).

Finally, while *automatic* and *named* modules cannot have a split package, the
*unnamed* module can have a package with the same name as another package in an
*automatic* module or a *named* module. This can be confusing. When this
happens, the Java Module System will simply ignore the package found in the
*unnamed* module and uses the package found in the *automatic* or *named*
module.

We have a simple program with four JAR files that do not specify the
`module-info.java` file.

- `domain-v1.jar`: contains the classes: `demo.domain.Quote` and
  `demo.domain.Formatter` classes. This represents an older version of a
  library.
- `domain-v2.jar`: contains the classes: `demo.domain.Quote` and
  `demo.domain.Formatter` classes. This represents the new version of the
  `domain-v1.jar` library, which adds a new method to the
  `demo.domain.Formatter` class.
- `db.jar`: represents a repository that returns the list of quotes. This
  depends on `domain-v1.jar` as it does not make use of the new method provided
  by `domain-v2.jar`. In other words, it has no reason to migrate ot the new
  version.
- `app.jar`: contains the `main()` method, in the class `demo.app.Main`, and
  acts as an entry point to the program. This depends on `db.jar` and
  `domain-v2.jar` and makes use of the new method to print the list of quotes
  returned by the repository.

The following table lists all packages and in which project these are found.

| Packages      | `domain-v1.jar` | `domain-v2.jar` | `db.jar` | `app.jar` | Split Package |
| ------------- | :-------------: | :-------------: | :------: | :-------: | :-----------: |
| `demo.app`    |       NO        |       NO        |    NO    |  **YES**  |      NO       |
| `demo.db`     |       NO        |       NO        | **YES**  |    NO     |      NO       |
| `demo.domain` |     **YES**     |     **YES**     |    NO    |    NO     |    **YES**    |

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR files

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── app.jar
   ├── db.jar
   ├── domain-v1.jar
   └── domain-v2.jar

   1 directory, 4 files
   ```

2. Run the application

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/app.jar:./target/libs/db.jar:./target/libs/domain-v1.jar:./target/libs/domain-v2.jar' \
     demo.app.Main
   ```

   In this case the `Formatter` from the `domain-v1.jar` JAR file is loaded and
   the application fails at runtime.

   ```
   1. Formatter.multiLine(Quote)
   "The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall."
   by Nelson Mandela

   2. Formatter.singleLine(Quote)
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'java.lang.String demo.domain.Formatter.singleLine(demo.domain.Quote)'
       at demo.app.Main.lambda$main$0(Main.java:17)
       at java.base/java.util.ImmutableCollections$List12.forEach(ImmutableCollections.java:681)
       at demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:11)
   ```

   Swap the order of the *domain* JAR files in the class path, and try again.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/app.jar:./target/libs/db.jar:./target/libs/domain-v2.jar:./target/libs/domain-v1.jar' \
     demo.app.Main
   ```

   This time the `Formatter` from the `domain-v2.jar` JAR file is loaded and
   the application worked as expected.

   ```
   1. Formatter.multiLine(Quote)
   "The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall."
   by Nelson Mandela

   2. Formatter.singleLine(Quote)
   The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall. by Nelson Mandela
   ```

   In this example, the second version (`domain-v2.jar`) did not include
   breaking changes, and is it safe to replace `domain-v1.jar` with
   `domain-v2.jar`. But there can be cases where the new version includes
   breaking changes and both JAR files are needed. In this case, it is ideal to
   move the library to a new package, say `demo.domain.v2`, so that this does
   not conflict with the earlier version and both can be safely loaded together.

   Note that the `--class-path` supports wildcards, as noted in the
   [Java man pages](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/java.html)

   > As a special convenience, a class path element that contains a base name of
   > an asterisk (`*`) is considered equivalent to specifying a list of all the
   > files in the directory with the extension `.jar` or `.JAR`. A Java program
   > can't tell the difference between the two invocations. For example, if the
   > directory `libs` contains `a.jar` and `b.JAR`, then the class path element
   > `libs/*` is expanded to `a.jar:b.JAR`, except that the order of JAR files
   > is **unspecified**. All `.jar` files in the specified directory, even
   > hidden ones, are included in the list. A class path entry consisting of an
   > asterisk (`*`) expands to a list of all the jar files in the current
   > directory.
   ([reference](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/java.html))

   For example

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.app.Main
   ```

   This **may** produce different results depending on the order in which the
   JAR files are expanded.

   ```
   1. Formatter.multiLine(Quote)
   "The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall."
   by Nelson Mandela

   2. Formatter.singleLine(Quote)
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'java.lang.String demo.domain.Formatter.singleLine(demo.domain.Quote)'
       at demo.app.Main.lambda$main$0(Main.java:17)
       at java.base/java.util.ImmutableCollections$List12.forEach(ImmutableCollections.java:681)
       at demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:11)
   ```
